rationale: The last cell of the comparison is in, and with it the condition reads consistently. Locally, a 100 ms tick period with a two-tick follower flush returned the correct index (returned 4, entry 33 at 4, decided values 11,12,22,33,34,35) and reported `decided_after_buffering` 2, i.e. the origin's two deferred entries had already been flushed and decided before the partition instead of sitting in its batch across the re-synchronisation. Reading all six retained runs and this one together with the source gives one condition rather than a tick-period band or a flush-deadline rule: the shift needs the origin's deferred entries to still be in its batch when the re-synchronisation truncates them, and the flush and the truncation to fall inside one tick window. That fits every cell: with the default hundred-tick flush deadline at 500 and 1000 ms ticks the deadline exceeded the run, so the entries were still queued and the Prepare's flush plus the following truncation shared a window, and the shift appeared; at 100 and 250 ms ticks the deadline fired before the re-synchronisation, so the entries had left the batch and no shift appeared; and with a two-tick flush deadline at either 1000 or 100 ms the entries were flushed long before, and no shift appeared. I record that as the corrected condition, append the account, and submit the new case so the last cell has a receipt.

investigations.discriminator: The condition is now stated so that all six configurations and the source agree, and the submitted case is the last cell; what remains unmeasured is the case where the origin's entries are discarded while its decided index also carries progress, which would show the mechanism's intermediate steps rather than only its endpoints.

knowledge.statement: When a re-synchronisation truncates entries whose deferred placeholders in `unconfirmed_local` are still queued, those placeholders keep their position and are consumed by later index advances, so the index reported for a later caller is shifted upward by the number of discarded entries. Retained evidence over six configurations: with the default hundred-tick flush deadline the shift appears at 500 and 1000 ms tick periods (index 4 while entry 33 sits at 2, or 3 while it sits at 1, with the returned index holding entry 35) and not at 100 or 250 ms; with a two-tick flush deadline it does not appear at 1000 ms or at 100 ms, and in the 100 ms case the origin's deferred entries were already decided before the partition.
knowledge.conditions: Actor layer with batch_size 3, three-node cluster, majority quorum, the leader cut off from both followers, the followers taking over with node 3, the origin re-elected explicitly, and a fresh `append_notify` filling the batch with two filler appends. The shift needs the origin's two entries to still be in its batch when the re-synchronisation truncates them (neither the batch filling nor the flush tick has removed them) and the flush and the truncation to fall inside one tick window, which is why it appears only where the flush deadline exceeds the run and the tick period exceeds the round trip. The internal placeholder queue is unobservable through the public API, so the queue accounting is the mechanism the endpoints imply rather than a direct observation, and no retained run exhibits the case where the origin's decided index also carries progress.
knowledge.changed_premise: The condition is now stated as what the six cells and the source jointly support rather than as a tick-period band or a flush-deadline rule: the origin's deferred entries must still be in its batch when the re-synchronisation truncates them and the flush and truncation must fall inside one tick window. The new cell (100 ms tick with a two-tick flush deadline) returned the correct index and showed the origin's entries already decided before the partition, which completes the comparison.

scope.description: One run of the lost-entry scenario at a 100 ms tick period with every node's flush-batch tick timeout set to two ticks instead of the default hundred, so the origin's two deferred entries are flushed early rather than sitting in its batch across the re-synchronisation. The run buffers two `append_notify` entries on the origin, cuts it off so the followers take over, restores the links, re-elects the origin, buffers a fresh entry 33 with two filler appends, and reports the returned index against the entry's true position together with the entry at the returned index and each node's decided values.
assumptions: Reducing `flush_batch_tick_timeout` changes only when a partially filled batch is flushed; it does not change the batch size, the quorum or the message flow.
The scenario, the measured quantities and the re-election step are identical to the earlier cases, so a difference in outcome is attributable to the tick period and the flush deadline.
No target logic is modified; the harness only configures the timeout through the public server config.
excluded: Any claim about batch sizes other than 3, or about the case where the origin's decided index carries progress.
Any claim about the internal placeholder queue, which is unobservable through the public API.
Any claim about tick periods or flush deadlines outside the six configurations measured.

experiment.prefix: Build three actors with batch_size 3, a 100 ms tick period and a flush-batch tick timeout of two ticks, node 1 carrying leader_priority 1. Elect node 1 and emit the admission event. Buffer `append_notify(11)` and `append_notify(12)` on node 1, sampling its decided index afterwards to record whether the entries were flushed and decided before the partition. Block node 1's links to nodes 2 and 3 both ways, wait until nodes 2 and 3 report a new leader, and call `append_notify(22)` on it. Unblock the links and sleep several ticks, recording the origin's decided index, its promise pid and its accept-phase flag. Call `try_become_leader()` on node 1 until it reports itself as the accepted leader, spawn `append_notify(33)` on it, follow with plain appends 34 and 35, sleep, and await the fresh call. Read node 1's decided suffix, find the 1-based position of entry 33 and the entry at the returned index, and emit the outcome with the resolution, both indices, whether they agree, the entry at the returned index and the decided values.
semantic_changes: The flush deadline became a parameter of the parameterised case and one case completes the two-by-two over tick period and flush deadline; existing cases are unchanged.
experiment.responsibility: The decisive inputs come from the target: the flush-batch timeout decides whether the origin's deferred entries are still queued when the re-synchronisation truncates them, the accept-sync valid-entries rule decides whether they are replaced, and `reconcile_unconfirmed` maps the surviving placeholders to index advances. The harness chooses the configuration and reads the endpoints.

comparisons.description: If the fresh call resolves Ok, the returned index must be the entry's true position. Locally this held with a fast flush at both tick periods, so a violation here would weaken the reading that the entries must still be queued at the truncation.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the flush deadline as a parameter of the parameterised case (it was fixed at the default hundred for every earlier case, and only the bespoke decoupling case varied it) and one case that runs the scenario at a 100 ms tick period with a two-tick flush deadline, completing the two-by-two over tick period and flush deadline. The existing cases and their comparisons are unchanged; a fresh execution is required because the harness bytes changed.
